ground_truth.description: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.root_cause: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet once, call deploy again → reverts. Attacker can front-run to cause DoS. PoC: test_factory_double_deploy_PoC in AuditPoC.sol. Shows first deploy succeeds, second reverts.
ground_truth.fix_description: Check if address exists via predicted.code.length, return it if so.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The deploy function uses CREATE2 to deploy wallet contracts but reverts with 'DeployFailed' when a contract already exists at the computed address. This violates ERC-4337 expectations where factories should return the existing address instead of reverting, breaking simulation and bundler logic.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. User calls deploy() with _mainModule and _salt to create a wallet 2. Same user or attacker calls deploy() again with same parameters 3. Function reverts instead of returning existing wallet address 4. This breaks ERC-4337 compliant bundlers that expect address return on duplicate deployment attempts
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Check if contract already exists at the predicted address using extcodesize before attempting deployment. If it exists, return the address directly. Otherwise, proceed with CREATE2 deployment.

prediction.overall_explanation: The factory contract has a denial-of-service vulnerability where repeated deployment attempts with the same parameters cause the function to revert instead of returning the existing contract address, breaking ERC-4337 compatibility expectations.
